config: hard joint-limit termination margin=0.05 rad + dof penalty reverted to -10 (baseline). 1500-iter. segigo1440.
headline: Hard termination at 0.05 rad margin drives the policy to avoid joint limits (dof penalty dropped 30x to -0.005) BUT at the cost of large lateral drift (4.05m, was 0.37m) and yaw drift (19.4 deg/s, was 1.1). The policy found a curved/yawing gait to avoid the tight limits. This is a WORSENING in the walking-task metrics vs the TASK_059 baseline.

comparison_vs_baseline_TASK_059.vx_err: 0.123 vs 0.244 — BETTER (the conservative policy tracks velocity more precisely)
comparison_vs_baseline_TASK_059.jp_err_analytic: 0.262 vs 0.221 — slightly higher but still PASS
comparison_vs_baseline_TASK_059.dof_viol: TBD from full report; training dof penalty dropped to -0.005 (vs -0.14), suggesting significant reduction

root_cause_analysis: The 0.05 rad hard-termination margin is too tight for the X1's conservative joint limits. The policy cannot learn to stay within ±0.05 rad of the tight limits (which are already narrow, e.g. hip_roll ±0.35) while also maintaining a stable straight gait. Instead it finds a LOCAL OPTIMUM: a curved/yawing walk that avoids hitting limits (hence dof penalty drops) but drifts laterally. This is the same safety-vs-performance tradeoff seen in iter-15 (-30 penalty degraded vx), now manifesting as degraded lateral/yaw stability instead.

experiment_summary_iter15_iter16.iter15_penalty_-30: dof penalty 3x stiffer: vx_err degraded (0.499 FAIL), dof insufficient
experiment_summary_iter15_iter16.iter16_hard_term_005: hard termination 0.05 rad: lat_drift degraded (4.05 FAIL), yaw_drift degraded (19.4 FAIL), dof likely reduced
experiment_summary_iter15_iter16.conclusion: BOTH approaches to driving dof_viol->0 create unacceptable tradeoffs in other metrics. The frozen dof_viol=0 threshold is very strict for a learned walking policy on a robot with conservative joint windows. The TASK_059 baseline (penalty -10, no hard termination) has the BEST OVERALL balance: vx_err 0.244 PASS, jp_err_analytic 0.221 PASS, lat_drift 0.37 PASS, yaw_drift 1.1 PASS, fall_rate 0 PASS — only dof_viol (30776) fails.

gateC_strategic_assessment.best_checkpoint: TASK_059 model_1500.pt (commit cd68a75, dof penalty -10, no hard termination). ALL metric groups PASS except dof_viol.
gateC_strategic_assessment.dof_viol_nature: The violations are small in magnitude (average ~0.014 rad over-limit, ~5% of joint-instances). They are PD-controller overshoot at the sim-step level, not a catastrophic policy defect.
gateC_strategic_assessment.threshold_assessment: The frozen dof_viol=0 threshold requires ZERO joint-limit violations across all 5 seeds × 4 episodes × 2401 steps × 12 joints = 576,240 joint-instances. This is extremely strict for any learned policy. The original task_spec set this threshold at first entry to amp_training (iteration 3) before the difficulty was known.
gateC_strategic_assessment.honest_conclusion: The F1/X1 AMP policy achieves STABLE, IMITATING walking with strong metrics across all groups. The only remaining Gate-C item (dof_viol=0) cannot be met by the current approaches without unacceptable degradation of other metrics. This is a genuine research limitation, not a metric error or a trivial fix.

next_directions.option_A_accept_document: Accept dof_viol>0 as a known limitation with quantified magnitude (~5% of joint-instances, ~0.014 rad average over-limit). Document honestly. Proceed to Sim2Sim. Gate C passes on all items except this one, with a clear explanation.
next_directions.option_B_wider_margin: Try hard termination at 0.15-0.20 rad (wider margin). This would allow the ~0.014 rad PD overshoot while catching only severe violations. May recover lat_drift/yaw_drift while still reducing dof_viol substantially (though not to exactly 0).
next_directions.option_C_longer_training: The 1500-iter budget may be insufficient for the policy to fully adapt to the constraint. A 3000+ iter run with hard termination might let the policy find a stable gait within limits. But this exceeds single-account budget.
next_directions.recommendation: Option B (wider margin 0.15) is the most promising single-variable experiment. If it reduces dof_viol to near-zero while retaining lat_drift/yaw_drift, Gate C can close. If not, Option A (document the quantified limitation) is the honest path.
